title: Cannot use CSS modules with bundle option
impact: bundle() users with cssModules who split one module across @import-ed files, and non-JS setups (Phoenix/Rails) wanting one CSS bundle plus per-file maps. Low engagement (1 reaction, 9 comments since 2022); #1034 (closed by reporter, not_planned) is the same root cause: imported file's classes missing from exports.
code: src/bundler.rs: Bundler (each file gets its own CSS modules hash/source index; only the entry's exports are returned)
summary: With bundle() + cssModules, every file is hashed separately, but only the entry file's classes are exported. So a class defined only in an @import-ed file is renamed but unreachable, and a class defined in both files gets two different names with only the entry's in the map. This matches neither the maintainer's stated design (imports behave as if written in the same file, i.e. same name, all exported) nor the reporter's request (one export map per file). Note: the 2022 report showed one shared name, so behavior changed to per-file hashing at or before 1.14.0.

Output: `.Jt5MtW_test`, `.Jt5MtW_only-in-app`, `._3uslJa_test`; exports `{"test":"_3uslJa_test"}`. check() encodes the maintainer's 2022 comment (same name, imported classes exported); control: entry's own class is exported.
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs local + 1.31.1..1.33.0 and --range 1.14.0..1.33.0: identical in every release, no change. Related: #1034 (same symptom), #273 (unrelated user error). The bundler's own test test_css_module in src/bundler.rs enshrines the current behavior (b.css `.a` -> `_9z6RGq_a`, exports only `a => _6lixEq_a`). Verified that transform() on app.css alone exports test -> Jt5MtW_test, the same name bundle() writes for that file.

fix.approach: Decide the model: (a) treat @import-ed files as part of the entry module (shared hash, merged exports; matches the 2022 maintainer comment and postcss-import+postcss-modules), or (b) return exports per source file (e.g. a map keyed by file, an additive JS API change). At minimum, document that only the entry's exports are returned, or warn.

draftReply:
Status update: on 1.33.0, `bundle()` with `cssModules` hashes each file separately, but only the entry file's classes appear in `exports`. With your example, `app.css`'s `.test` becomes a different name from `index.css`'s `.test`, and classes that exist only in `app.css` don't appear in the exports at all (same as #1034). That isn't what either of the options discussed above would produce, so this needs a decision on which model to support: imported files sharing the entry's module scope, or an export map per file. Until then, run `transform()` on each module file to get its own exports, and use `bundle()` with the same `cssModules` config only for the combined CSS. With the same filename (and `projectRoot`, if you set one), the class names match what `bundle()` writes.
